benchmark_kind: corruption threshold versus committee size: what 2-collusion tolerance actually costs
scope_warning: A single radix_sort kernel (1024 rows, 16-bit keys) on one host, not the retrieval circuit. All parties ran on one machine, which does not instantiate any non-collusion assumption. The 5-party configuration is NOT implemented in this codebase: the sharing, assembly, and circuits are all hardcoded to three servers. These figures size an option, they do not report a working system. Passive protocols only.
question: The project declares a 3-server, any-2-may-collude threat model, which forces dishonest-majority MPC and costs 261x on the growing term. Is there a configuration with the SAME 2-collusion tolerance that does not pay it?
the_observation: Tolerating t corruptions needs dishonest-majority protocols only when t >= n/2. With n=3 and t=2 that holds, so Semi is required. With n=5 and t=2, 2 < 2.5, so honest majority holds and cheap protocols apply -- at the same absolute collusion tolerance.

headline.comparison: semi_3_parties versus atlas_5_parties, which tolerate the SAME absolute number of colluding servers
headline.reading: Adding two more servers converts a dishonest majority of three into an honest majority of five, keeping 2-collusion tolerance while removing the dishonest-majority protocol premium almost entirely.

the_honest_caveat.not_a_free_lunch: The two configurations are equivalent in absolute collusion tolerance but NOT in the fraction of the committee that must stay honest. Three-party Semi needs only 1 of 3 honest (33%); five-party ATLAS needs 3 of 5 honest (60%). Three-party Semi therefore fails only if EVERY server is corrupt, which remains the strongest possible guarantee for a three-server committee.
the_honest_caveat.which_matters_depends_on_deployment: If the federation can field five independently administered servers and believes at most two will collude, five-party honest majority gives the same protection for about 1/126th of the communication. If only three candidate operators exist, the option does not apply.
the_honest_caveat.operational_cost: Five servers means five sets of shares, five deployments, five audit relationships. That is a real governance cost this benchmark does not price.

possible_second_benefit_unverified.claim: Information-theoretic t-private PIR with k servers has communication about N^(1/floor((k-1)/t)). For k=3, t=2 the exponent is 1, i.e. linear. For k=5, t=2 it is 1/2, i.e. square-root.
possible_second_benefit_unverified.consequence_if_true: Moving to five servers would not merely cut constants; it would unblock sublinear dependent reads, which benchmarks/doram_viability_under_dishonest_majority.json shows are unreachable at k=3, t=2.
possible_second_benefit_unverified.status: NOT VERIFIED. Recalled from the PIR literature and not confirmed against primary sources in this session. It is the single highest-value thing to check before committing to a committee size.

what_this_does_not_show: Any measurement of the retrieval circuit at five parties; only a sorting kernel was run.
A working five-party implementation; the codebase is hardcoded to three servers throughout.
Any real dataset, WAN, or multi-host result.
That five independently administered servers are available in the target deployment.
